terms.gloss: oneself, referring to a general subject
terms.grammar: pronoun, reflexive: genitive suī, dative sibi, accusative and ablative sē; the same for every gender and number
evidence: Cic. Sen. 49: sēcum esse sēcumque … vīvere
Cic. Off. 2.64: paulum nōn numquam dē suō jūre dēcēdere
terms.comment: With an infinitive or a general subject (quisque, “everyone”) the reflexive is the same sē, and the possessive suus: sēcum vīvere, to live with oneself; dē suō jūre dēcēdere, to give up some of one’s rights.
As in “to do it oneself”: sē ipsum fēlīcem facit.

phrases.latin: sēcum esse sēcumque, ut dīcitur, vīvere
phrases.english: to be with oneself and, as they say, to live with oneself

phrases.latin: est enim nōn modo līberāle paulum nōn numquam dē suō jūre dēcēdere, sed interdum etiam frūctuōsum
phrases.english: For it is not only generous now and then to give up a little of one’s rights, but sometimes profitable too.

phrases.latin: Quod quisque amat, laudandō commendat sibi.
phrases.english: What one loves, one makes dearer to oneself by praising it.

phrases.latin: suō enim quisque studiō maximē dūcitur
phrases.english: For each of us is led most by his own interest.

sources: Lewis & Short: sui · Lewis & Short: ipse
